 Dated this the 5th day of June, 2025  ORDER
This bail application is filed under section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (for short 'BNSS').

2. Petitioner is the fourth accused in Crime No.560 of 2024 of Kanjaar Police Station, Idukki,
registered for the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
3. According to the prosecution, accused 1 and 2 were running a consultancy by name and style "Columbus Jobs and Education" and they promised to arrange a job visa for the defacto complainant in UK, and collected an amount of Rs.3 lakhs from the defacto complainant.

However,
they failed to provide the employment or return the entire amount except for Rs. 1 lakh, and thus the accused together committed the offences alleged.

4. I have heard Sri. Saju K. T., the learned counsel for the petitioner as well as Sri. Noushad K. A.,
the learned Public Prosecutor.

5. The learned Public Prosecutor, upon instructions, submitted that petitioner is now arrayed as the first accused in the above crime and that he had collected 3 lakhs rupees from the defacto complainant 2025:KER:39619 and returned only Rs. 1 lakh, without providing the employment promised.

6. On a perusal of the FIR as well as on an appreciation of the contentions raised, it is noticed that the petitioner is alleged to have promised an employment to the defacto complainant and collected amounts from him.
However, since the employment could not be obtained, he returned a portion of the amount.
Since prima facie the ingredients of the offence alleged are not seen to be made out, I am of the view that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is not necessary.

Accordingly, this application is allowed on the following conditions:
(a) Petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer on 12.06.2025 and shall subject himself to interrogation.

(b) If after interrogation, the Investigating Officer proposes to arrest the petitioner,
then, he shall be released on bail on him executing a bond for Rs.50,000/- (Rupees fifty thousand only) with two solvent sureties each for the like sum before the Investigating Officer.

(d) Petitioner shall not intimidate or attempt to 2025:KER:39619 influence the witnesses; nor shall they tamper with the evidence.
(e) Petitioner shall not commit any similar offences while he is on bail.

In case of violation of any of the above conditions or if any modification or deletion of the conditions are required, the jurisdictional Court shall be empowered to consider such applications, if any, and pass appropriate orders in accordance with the law, notwithstanding the bail having been granted by this Court.
